sources.title: Guinea-Bissau Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Current diagnostics and modeled climate, mobility and development effects through 2050 and 2100
sources.methodology: Country climate-development diagnostic with modeled impacts and fragility review.
sources.limitations: National analysis; some local and farmer-herder links are conditional.

sources.title: The Sea Swallowed our Houses and Rice Fields: The Vulnerability to Climate Change of Coastal People in Guinea-Bissau, West Africa
sources.organization: Marina Padrão Temudo and Ana I. R. Cabral, University of Lisbon; Pedro Reis, National Institute of Agricultural and Veterinary Research
sources.temporal_coverage: Djobel household survey in 2017; Diola livelihoods research 2017–2019 and follow-up fieldwork through 2022
sources.methodology: All-household Djobel survey, interviews across five villages, repeated fieldwork and land-cover mapping.
sources.limitations: Single island-village case; conflict history includes qualitative accounts and cited earlier records.

sources.title: Guinea-Bissau country strategic plan (2023–2027)
sources.temporal_coverage: Country analysis and prior flood impacts; planned WFP programming for 2023–2027
sources.methodology: WFP country plan informed by country analysis and partner consultations in May 2022.
sources.limitations: Plan commitments are not implementation or impact evidence; cited flood totals are not locally disaggregated.

sources.title: Country Hydromet Diagnostics: Guinea-Bissau Peer Review Report
sources.organization: Systematic Observations Financing Facility and World Meteorological Organization, with Guinea-Bissau National Meteorological Institute
sources.temporal_coverage: Hydrometeorological-service capacity and observation network, assessed in 2024
sources.methodology: Standardized WMO Country Hydromet Diagnostics using national-service information and peer review.
sources.limitations: National service diagnostic; it does not measure community receipt of forecasts or warnings.

claims.locator: PDF p. 17, section 1.2.2, climate change impacts on human development
claims.paraphrase: CCDR projects climate change may send pastoralists farther for grazing, potentially heightening existing tensions between farmers and cattle owners.
claims.scenario: Qualitative future statement; local scenario and timing are unspecified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Longer climate-driven grazing trips may heighten farmer–cattle-owner tensions (PDF p. 17).

claims.locator: PDF p. 20, section 1.2.5, climate change and migration
claims.paraphrase: CCDR says rising seas are forcing Djobel to retreat from the coast and reigniting historical interethnic conflicts over land use and resources.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Sea-level retreat is reigniting interethnic land and resource conflicts in Djobel (PDF p. 20).

claims.locator: PDF p. 18, section 1.2.3, transport and climate impacts
claims.paraphrase: Flooding puts national roads N1, N2 and N5 at risk; rainy-season road impassability restricts rural access to markets, water, schools and health care, especially for women.
claims.limitations: The report names corridors but gives no segment-level exposure counts here.

claims.locator: PDF p. 26, section 2.2, national strategies and plans
claims.paraphrase: CCDR says political instability challenges implementation and sustainability of comprehensive strategies for climate impacts and development needs.
claims.limitations: National diagnosis, without local delivery measures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says political instability impedes climate-strategy implementation (PDF p. 26).

claims.locator: Results, Djobel livelihoods and land-use section, 2017 rainy-season impacts
claims.paraphrase: In Djobel, 2017 storm surges, heavy rain and high-tide waves destroyed most rice-field infrastructure; ten families became houseless and damaged dikes left some children travelling to school by canoe or swimming.
claims.limitations: Local study account, not a national flood-loss estimate.

claims.locator: Abstract and Introduction, Djobel upland adaptation and land dispute
claims.paraphrase: The study says neighboring Arame's seizure of Djobel's upland territory hampered residents' efforts to adapt and establish safer settlement space.
claims.limitations: Qualitative case evidence; it does not isolate climate change as the cause of the land dispute.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Arame's land seizure hampered Djobel's climate adaptation (abstract).

claims.paraphrase: After years of requests for assistance and the 2017 flood and dike rupture, the authors report no effective technical or financial support for climate adaptation from state, NGOs or donors.
claims.limitations: Authors' case account, not a systematic response-performance evaluation.

claims.locator: Results, mangrove-rice farming and Djobel livelihoods
claims.paraphrase: Most young people return to Djobel seasonally for field work, leaving dike repair and maintenance to a diminishing number who stay.
claims.limitations: No assessment of current dike effectiveness.

claims.paraphrase: WFP reports that floods since 2015 affected over 170,000 people in southern coastal zones and eastern plains and destroyed 8 percent of total rice production.
claims.limitations: WFP cites the national service; period totals are not broken down by locality.

claims.locator: PDF p. 14, paragraph 68, planned climate-resilience activities
claims.paraphrase: WFP plans community watershed, water, climate-smart agriculture and forest/mangrove management for rural resilience, including women and young farmers.
claims.scenario: WFP country-plan commitments for 2023–2027; no results are reported at this locator.
claims.limitations: Planned activities, not delivered outcomes or evidence of reduced conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: WFP says asset creation and natural-resource management can reduce inter- and intracommunal conflict from resource scarcity (PDF p. 14).

claims.paraphrase: WFP reports only 0.9 percent of the population received a social-protection benefit; the 88-island geography further hinders universal service coverage for hard-to-reach communities.
claims.limitations: WFP cites 2022-era coverage; no post-2022 update is assessed here.

claims.paraphrase: INM-GB operated 19 classic weather stations, only 8 operational and none automatic; Bissau Airport, Bolama and Bafatá issued observations every three hours during daytime.
claims.limitations: Station counts do not show forecast receipt or last-mile reach.

claims.locator: PDF p. 5, executive summary; PDF p. 10, project implementation assessment
claims.paraphrase: The diagnostic rates overall INM-GB capacity at level 1 and says financial constraints and political instability stalled or discontinued some hydromet projects.
affected_groups: communities relying on public weather services
claims.limitations: The diagnostic does not estimate the amount of service disruption caused.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report attributes low project progress and discontinuation partly to political instability (PDF p. 10).

search_audit.query: Guinea-Bissau subnational climate vulnerability Bissau Bijagós flood drought adaptation report localities PDF government UN
search_audit.outcome: Opened the CCDR, WFP plan, hydromet diagnostic and Djobel study. They add named road corridors, eastern rainfall zones, southern/eastern flood exposure and village-level evidence.

search_audit.query: Guinea-Bissau climate conflict natural resources fisheries land water security fragility report Bijagós farmer conflict
search_audit.outcome: The CCDR explicitly links longer climate-driven grazing trips with farmer-herder tensions and sea-level retreat in Djobel with land/resource conflicts; the Djobel article documents local land access conflict. These are not national violence estimates.

search_audit.query: Guinea-Bissau political instability conflict humanitarian access climate adaptation disaster response disruption report
search_audit.outcome: The Djobel study says neighboring land seizure hampered adaptation; the hydromet diagnostic says instability stalled or discontinued some projects. No opened source established a national armed-conflict disruption of humanitarian access; this is an evidence gap.

search_audit.query: Guinea-Bissau community disaster risk early warning preparedness resilience capacity flood response assessment PDF
search_audit.outcome: The hydromet report quantifies station capacity; WFP plans last-mile information and community watershed work; the Djobel study describes customary dike and water-management knowledge and its labor constraints.

gaps: The UN Common Country Analysis PDF returned HTTP 530 and the UNICEF 2025 regional situation report exceeded browser size limits; no claims use search-indexed text from either source.
The Djobel research is a detailed single-village case and should not be generalized to Guinea-Bissau; conflict history includes qualitative accounts and cited historical records.
The CCDR's farmer-herder and Djobel pathways are source-stated but do not provide local conflict incidence or independently estimate climate attribution.
The hydromet diagnostic and WFP plan document capacity constraints and commitments, but not the current reach or effectiveness of last-mile warnings and services.
